newsitem.title: USA: Sunshine edging back into western U.S. Corn Belt.
newsitem.headline: Sunshine edging back into western U.S. Corn Belt.

text.p: Sunshine was slowly beginning to return to western portions of the U.S. Midwest on Wednesday but the prospects for significant progress with corn and soybean harvests appeared dim, meteorologists said.

"Sunshine is already here in Omaha and we should see gradually improving conditions across Iowa today (Wednesday) and tomorrow should be sunny," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Nebraska-based Weather Express Inc.
Gesser said, however, conditions may not dry out enough to allow farmers to return to fields before the next rain-bearing system arrives around the weekend.
He noted 80 percent of Iowa had between 0.75 and 2.00 inches of rain in the last 24 to 36 hours, with only the northwest corner around Sioux City escaping.
Gesser said that there would be additional showers on Wednesday of up to 0.75 inches in northeast Illinois, Indiana and Ohio although Iowa and Nebraska should be dry.

Joel Burgio, agricultural meteorologist for Weather Services Corp, said harvesting prospects appeared brightest in the southeast belt (south-central Ohio, south-cental Indiana and south-east Illinois) where rainfall had been lightest.
Some of those areas had less than 0.50 inch, he added.
Burgio said, however, a system currently in the U.S. Delta could possibly bring rain to the southeast Corn Belt as early as Friday. It may, however, not reach that far north.

A more important rain-bearing system should spread across the Corn Belt over the weekend, starting in western regions early Saturday and reaching the Ohio Valley on Monday, Weather Services Corp's Burgio said.
Snow which covered northeast Kansas, southeast Nebraska, southwest Iowa and northwest Missouri on Tuesday looked set to quickly disappear. Six to eight inches fell in some parts of northeast Kansas.
"It will be in the 60s (degrees Fahrenheit) in Kansas today so it should be gone by the time the day is out," WSC's Burgio said of expectations for the unusually early snow to melt Wednesday.
